links.outcome: Readability of LLM-generated AIH patient education text relative to general patient reading level
links.effect: Relatively high readability levels across models suggest further simplification may be needed for general patient populations; disease mechanism and diagnostic content showed higher linguistic complexity.
links.quote: Although most models produced moderate-to-good quality information, relatively high readability levels suggest that further simplification may be needed for general patient populations.

links.outcome: Plain-language comprehensibility of LLM-generated patient education content
links.effect: Readability varied significantly across content themes, with disease mechanism and diagnostic texts showing higher linguistic complexity; models differed significantly in readability, quality and suitability (all p < 0.05).
links.quote: Readability varied significantly across content themes, with texts related to disease mechanisms and diagnostic processes exhibiting higher linguistic complexity.

screen.reason: The study empirically evaluates five mainstream LLMs across readability, quality, and clinical intent alignment metrics for autoimmune hepatitis patient education questions, without testing a specific deployment practice or safeguard.
